1	#!/bin/bash
2	
3	set -euo pipefail
4	
5	GITHUB_REPO="entireio/cli"
6	DEFAULT_INSTALL_DIR="$HOME/.local/bin"
7	DEFAULT_CHANNEL="stable"
8	
9	# Colors (disabled in non-interactive mode)
10	if [[ -t 1 ]]; then
11	    RED='\033[0;31m'
12	    GREEN='\033[0;32m'
13	    YELLOW='\033[0;33m'
14	    BLUE='\033[0;34m'
15	    BOLD='\033[1m'
16	    NC='\033[0m' # No Color
17	else
18	    RED=''
19	    GREEN=''
20	    YELLOW=''
21	    BLUE=''
22	    BOLD=''
23	    NC=''
24	fi
25	
26	info() {
27	    printf '%b%s%b\n' "${BLUE}==>${NC} ${BOLD}" "$1" "${NC}"
28	}
29	
30	success() {
31	    printf '%b%s%b\n' "${GREEN}==>${NC} ${BOLD}" "$1" "${NC}"
32	}
33	
34	warn() {
35	    printf '%b %s\n' "${YELLOW}Warning:${NC}" "$1"
36	}
37	
38	error() {
39	    printf '%b %s\n' "${RED}Error:${NC}" "$1" >&2
40	    exit 1
41	}
42	
43	usage() {
44	    cat <<EOF
45	Usage: install.sh [--channel stable|nightly]
46	
47	Options:
48	  --channel   Release channel to install (default: stable)
49	  -h, --help  Show this help message
50	EOF
51	}
52	
53	detect_os() {
54	    local os
55	    os="$(uname -s | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"
56	    case "$os" in
57	        darwin)
58	            echo "darwin"
59	            ;;
60	        linux)
61	            echo "linux"
62	            ;;
63	        mingw*|msys*|cygwin*)
64	            error "install.sh does not support Windows, you can install the Entire CLI using scoop:
65	
66	    scoop install entire/cli
67	
68	  Or download the Windows zip from:
69	    https://github.com/entireio/cli/releases/latest"
70	            ;;
71	        *)
72	            error "Unsupported operating system: $os"
73	            ;;
74	    esac
75	}
76	
77	detect_arch() {
78	    local arch
79	    arch="$(uname -m)"
80	    case "$arch" in
81	        x86_64|amd64)
82	            echo "amd64"
83	            ;;
84	        arm64|aarch64)
85	            echo "arm64"
86	            ;;
87	        *)
88	            error "Unsupported architecture: $arch"
89	            ;;
90	    esac
91	}
92	
93	fetch_github_json() {
94	    local url="$1"
95	    local curl_opts=(-fsSL)
96	    if [[ -n "${GITHUB_TOKEN:-}" ]]; then
97	        curl_opts+=(-H "Authorization: Bearer ${GITHUB_TOKEN}")
98	    fi
99	
100	    curl "${curl_opts[@]}" "$url" 2>/dev/null
101	}
102	
103	get_latest_stable_version() {
104	    local url="https://api.github.com/repos/${GITHUB_REPO}/releases/latest"
105	    local version
106	    version=$(fetch_github_json "$url" | grep '"tag_name"' | sed -E 's/.*"tag_name": *"v?([^"]+)".*/\1/')
107	
108	    if [[ -z "$version" ]]; then
109	        error "Failed to fetch latest version from GitHub. Please check your internet connection."
110	    fi
111	
112	    echo "$version"
113	}
114	
115	get_latest_nightly_version() {
116	    local url="https://api.github.com/repos/${GITHUB_REPO}/releases?per_page=20"
117	    local version
118	    version=$(fetch_github_json "$url" | grep '"tag_name"' | grep 'nightly' | head -n 1 | sed -E 's/.*"tag_name": *"v?([^"]+)".*/\1/')
119	
120	    if [[ -z "$version" ]]; then
121	        error "Failed to fetch latest nightly version from GitHub. Please check your internet connection."
122	    fi
123	
124	    echo "$version"
125	}
126	
127	download_file() {
128	    local url="$1"
129	    local output="$2"
130	    local curl_opts=(-fsSL)
131	
132	    curl "${curl_opts[@]}" "$url" -o "$output"
133	}
134	
135	verify_checksum() {
136	    local file="$1"
137	    local expected_checksum="$2"
138	    local actual_checksum
139	
140	    if command -v sha256sum &> /dev/null; then
141	        actual_checksum=$(sha256sum "$file" | awk '{print $1}')
142	    elif command -v shasum &> /dev/null; then
143	        actual_checksum=$(shasum -a 256 "$file" | awk '{print $1}')
144	    else
145	        warn "No checksum tool found (sha256sum or shasum). Skipping verification."
146	        return 0
147	    fi
148	
149	    if [[ "$actual_checksum" != "$expected_checksum" ]]; then
150	        error "Checksum verification failed!  Expected: $expected_checksum, actual: $actual_checksum"
151	    fi
152	}
153	
154	main() {
155	    local channel="${DEFAULT_CHANNEL}"
156	    local version=""
157	
158	    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
159	        case "$1" in
160	            --channel)
161	                shift
162	                [[ $# -gt 0 ]] || error "--channel requires a value"
163	                channel="$1"
164	                ;;
165	            -h|--help)
166	                usage
167	                exit 0
168	                ;;
169	            *)
170	                error "Unknown argument: $1"
171	                ;;
172	        esac
173	        shift
174	    done
175	
176	    if ! command -v curl &> /dev/null; then
177	        error "curl is required but not installed. Please install curl and try again."
178	    fi
179	
180	    case "$channel" in
181	        stable|nightly) ;;
182	        *)
183	            error "Unsupported channel: ${channel}. Expected 'stable' or 'nightly'."
184	            ;;
185	    esac
186	
187	    info "Installing Entire CLI..."
188	
189	    # Detect platform
190	    local os arch
191	    os=$(detect_os)
192	    arch=$(detect_arch)
193	    info "Detected platform: ${os}/${arch}"
194	
195	    info "Fetching latest ${channel} version..."
196	    if [[ "$channel" == "nightly" ]]; then
197	        version=$(get_latest_nightly_version)
198	    else
199	        version=$(get_latest_stable_version)
200	    fi
201	    # Strip leading 'v' if present
202	    version="${version#v}"
203	    info "Installing version: ${version}"
204	
205	    # Construct download URL
206	    local archive_name="entire_${os}_${arch}.tar.gz"
207	    local download_url="https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPO}/releases/download/v${version}/${archive_name}"
208	    local checksums_url="https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPO}/releases/download/v${version}/checksums.txt"
209	
210	    tmp_dir=$(mktemp -d)
211	    trap 'rm -rf "$tmp_dir"' EXIT
212	
213	    # Download archive
214	    local archive_path="${tmp_dir}/${archive_name}"
215	    info "Downloading ${archive_name}..."
216	    if ! download_file "$download_url" "$archive_path"; then
217	        error "Failed to download from ${download_url}. Please check that the version exists and try again."
218	    fi
219	
220	    # Download and verify checksums
221	    info "Downloading checksums..."
222	    local checksums_path="${tmp_dir}/checksums.txt"
223	    if ! download_file "$checksums_url" "$checksums_path"; then
224	        error "Failed to download checksums from ${checksums_url}"
225	    fi
226	
227	    info "Verifying checksum..."
228	    local expected_checksum
229	    expected_checksum=$(grep -iE "${archive_name}\$" "$checksums_path" | awk '{print $1}' || true)
230	    if [[ -z "$expected_checksum" ]]; then
231	        error "Checksum for ${archive_name} not found in checksums.txt"
232	    fi
233	    verify_checksum "$archive_path" "$expected_checksum"
234	    success "Checksum verified"
235	
236	    info "Extracting..."
237	    tar -xzf "$archive_path" -C "$tmp_dir"
238	
239	    local install_dir="${DEFAULT_INSTALL_DIR}"
240	    local binary_path="${tmp_dir}/entire"
241	
242	    chmod +x "$binary_path"
243	
244	    info "Installing to ${install_dir}..."
245	    local install_path="${install_dir}/entire"
246	
247	    mkdir -p "${install_dir}"
248	    info "Directory ready"
249	
250	    if [[ ! -w "$install_dir" ]]; then
251	        error "Cannot write to ${install_dir}."
252	    fi
253	    mv "$binary_path" "$install_path"
254	
255	    # Install the git remote helper binary alongside entire so
256	    # `git clone entire://…` resolves it on PATH. It ships in the same
257	    # archive as a separate binary.
258	    if [[ -f "${tmp_dir}/git-remote-entire" ]]; then
259	        chmod +x "${tmp_dir}/git-remote-entire"
260	        mv "${tmp_dir}/git-remote-entire" "${install_dir}/git-remote-entire"
261	    else
262	        warn "git-remote-entire not found in archive; entire:// clones won't work until the next release includes it."
263	    fi
264

#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

GITHUB_REPO="entireio/cli"
DEFAULT_INSTALL_DIR="$HOME/.local/bin"
DEFAULT_CHANNEL="stable"

# Colors (disabled in non-interactive mode)
if [[ -t 1 ]]; then
    RED='\033[0;31m'
    GREEN='\033[0;32m'
    YELLOW='\033[0;33m'
    BLUE='\033[0;34m'
    BOLD='\033[1m'
    NC='\033[0m' # No Color
else
    RED=''
    GREEN=''
    YELLOW=''
    BLUE=''
    BOLD=''
    NC=''
fi

info() {
    printf '%b%s%b\n' "${BLUE}==>${NC} ${BOLD}" "$1" "${NC}"
}

success() {
    printf '%b%s%b\n' "${GREEN}==>${NC} ${BOLD}" "$1" "${NC}"
}

warn() {
    printf '%b %s\n' "${YELLOW}Warning:${NC}" "$1"
}

error() {
    printf '%b %s\n' "${RED}Error:${NC}" "$1" >&2
    exit 1
}

usage() {
    cat <<EOF
Usage: install.sh [--channel stable|nightly]

Options:
  --channel   Release channel to install (default: stable)
  -h, --help  Show this help message
EOF
}

detect_os() {
    local os
    os="$(uname -s | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"
    case "$os" in
        darwin)
            echo "darwin"
            ;;
        linux)
            echo "linux"
            ;;
        mingw*|msys*|cygwin*)
            error "install.sh does not support Windows, you can install the Entire CLI using scoop:

    scoop install entire/cli

  Or download the Windows zip from:
    https://github.com/entireio/cli/releases/latest"
            ;;
        *)
            error "Unsupported operating system: $os"
            ;;
    esac
}

detect_arch() {
    local arch
    arch="$(uname -m)"
    case "$arch" in
        x86_64|amd64)
            echo "amd64"
            ;;
        arm64|aarch64)
            echo "arm64"
            ;;
        *)
            error "Unsupported architecture: $arch"
            ;;
    esac
}

fetch_github_json() {
    local url="$1"
    local curl_opts=(-fsSL)
    if [[ -n "${GITHUB_TOKEN:-}" ]]; then
        curl_opts+=(-H "Authorization: Bearer ${GITHUB_TOKEN}")
    fi

    curl "${curl_opts[@]}" "$url" 2>/dev/null
}

get_latest_stable_version() {
    local url="https://api.github.com/repos/${GITHUB_REPO}/releases/latest"
    local version
    version=$(fetch_github_json "$url" | grep '"tag_name"' | sed -E 's/.*"tag_name": *"v?([^"]+)".*/\1/')

    if [[ -z "$version" ]]; then
        error "Failed to fetch latest version from GitHub. Please check your internet connection."
    fi

    echo "$version"
}

get_latest_nightly_version() {
    local url="https://api.github.com/repos/${GITHUB_REPO}/releases?per_page=20"
    local version
    version=$(fetch_github_json "$url" | grep '"tag_name"' | grep 'nightly' | head -n 1 | sed -E 's/.*"tag_name": *"v?([^"]+)".*/\1/')

    if [[ -z "$version" ]]; then
        error "Failed to fetch latest nightly version from GitHub. Please check your internet connection."
    fi

    echo "$version"
}

download_file() {
    local url="$1"
    local output="$2"
    local curl_opts=(-fsSL)

    curl "${curl_opts[@]}" "$url" -o "$output"
}

verify_checksum() {
    local file="$1"
    local expected_checksum="$2"
    local actual_checksum

    if command -v sha256sum &> /dev/null; then
        actual_checksum=$(sha256sum "$file" | awk '{print $1}')
    elif command -v shasum &> /dev/null; then
        actual_checksum=$(shasum -a 256 "$file" | awk '{print $1}')
    else
        warn "No checksum tool found (sha256sum or shasum). Skipping verification."
        return 0
    fi

    if [[ "$actual_checksum" != "$expected_checksum" ]]; then
        error "Checksum verification failed!  Expected: $expected_checksum, actual: $actual_checksum"
    fi
}

main() {
    local channel="${DEFAULT_CHANNEL}"
    local version=""

    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
        case "$1" in
            --channel)
                shift
                [[ $# -gt 0 ]] || error "--channel requires a value"
                channel="$1"
                ;;
            -h|--help)
                usage
                exit 0
                ;;
            *)
                error "Unknown argument: $1"
                ;;
        esac
        shift
    done

    if ! command -v curl &> /dev/null; then
        error "curl is required but not installed. Please install curl and try again."
    fi

    case "$channel" in
        stable|nightly) ;;
        *)
            error "Unsupported channel: ${channel}. Expected 'stable' or 'nightly'."
            ;;
    esac

    info "Installing Entire CLI..."

    # Detect platform
    local os arch
    os=$(detect_os)
    arch=$(detect_arch)
    info "Detected platform: ${os}/${arch}"

    info "Fetching latest ${channel} version..."
    if [[ "$channel" == "nightly" ]]; then
        version=$(get_latest_nightly_version)
    else
        version=$(get_latest_stable_version)
    fi
    # Strip leading 'v' if present
    version="${version#v}"
    info "Installing version: ${version}"

    # Construct download URL
    local archive_name="entire_${os}_${arch}.tar.gz"
    local download_url="https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPO}/releases/download/v${version}/${archive_name}"
    local checksums_url="https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPO}/releases/download/v${version}/checksums.txt"

    tmp_dir=$(mktemp -d)
    trap 'rm -rf "$tmp_dir"' EXIT

    # Download archive
    local archive_path="${tmp_dir}/${archive_name}"
    info "Downloading ${archive_name}..."
    if ! download_file "$download_url" "$archive_path"; then
        error "Failed to download from ${download_url}. Please check that the version exists and try again."
    fi

    # Download and verify checksums
    info "Downloading checksums..."
    local checksums_path="${tmp_dir}/checksums.txt"
    if ! download_file "$checksums_url" "$checksums_path"; then
        error "Failed to download checksums from ${checksums_url}"
    fi

    info "Verifying checksum..."
    local expected_checksum
    expected_checksum=$(grep -iE "${archive_name}\$" "$checksums_path" | awk '{print $1}' || true)
    if [[ -z "$expected_checksum" ]]; then
        error "Checksum for ${archive_name} not found in checksums.txt"
    fi
    verify_checksum "$archive_path" "$expected_checksum"
    success "Checksum verified"

    info "Extracting..."
    tar -xzf "$archive_path" -C "$tmp_dir"

    local install_dir="${DEFAULT_INSTALL_DIR}"
    local binary_path="${tmp_dir}/entire"

    chmod +x "$binary_path"

    info "Installing to ${install_dir}..."
    local install_path="${install_dir}/entire"

    mkdir -p "${install_dir}"
    info "Directory ready"

    if [[ ! -w "$install_dir" ]]; then
        error "Cannot write to ${install_dir}."
    fi
    mv "$binary_path" "$install_path"

    # Install the git remote helper binary alongside entire so
    # `git clone entire://…` resolves it on PATH. It ships in the same
    # archive as a separate binary.
    if [[ -f "${tmp_dir}/git-remote-entire" ]]; then
        chmod +x "${tmp_dir}/git-remote-entire"
        mv "${tmp_dir}/git-remote-entire" "${install_dir}/git-remote-entire"
    else
        warn "git-remote-entire not found in archive; entire:// clones won't work until the next release includes it."
    fi

    # Verify installation
    if "$install_path" version &> /dev/null; then
        success "Entire CLI installed to ${install_path}"
    else
        error "Installation completed but the binary failed to execute. Please check the installation."
    fi

    # Check if the installed binary is the one that will be found in PATH
    local path_binary
    path_binary=$(command -v "entire" 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [[ -n "$path_binary" && ! "$path_binary" -ef "$install_path" ]]; then
        # This case is a bit weird, because some other 'entire' is found on PATH.  Warn user.
        echo ""
        echo -e "${YELLOW}!${NC} ${BOLD}WARNING: PATH conflict detected${NC}"
        echo -e "${YELLOW}!${NC}"
        echo -e "${YELLOW}!${NC} Installed to: ${install_path}"
        echo -e "${YELLOW}!${NC} But 'entire' resolves to: ${path_binary}"
        echo -e "${YELLOW}!${NC}"
        echo -e "${YELLOW}!${NC} Your PATH may have another version of Entire CLI. To fix:"
        echo -e "${YELLOW}!${NC}   1. Remove the old binary: rm ${path_binary}"
        echo -e "${YELLOW}!${NC}   or"
        echo -e "${YELLOW}!${NC}   2. Adjust your PATH to prioritize ${install_dir}"
        echo ""
        error "Installation completed but PATH needs adjustment. Then, rerun the installation."
    elif [[ -z "$path_binary" ]]; then
        # First-time install: ~/.local/bin likely isn't on their PATH yet.
        # Detect their shell and show the right config file.
        local shell_name shell_config
        shell_name="$(basename "${SHELL:-}")"
        case "$shell_name" in
            zsh)
                # shellcheck disable=SC2088
                shell_config="~/.zshrc" ;;
            bash)
                if [[ -f "$HOME/.bash_profile" ]]; then
                    # shellcheck disable=SC2088
                    shell_config="~/.bash_profile"
                else
                    # shellcheck disable=SC2088
                    shell_config="~/.bashrc"
                fi
                ;;
            fish)
                # shellcheck disable=SC2088
                shell_config="~/.config/fish/config.fish" ;;
            *)
                shell_config="" ;;
        esac

        echo ""
        echo -e "  Add ${BOLD}entire${NC} to your PATH:"
        echo ""
        if [[ "$shell_name" == "fish" ]]; then
            echo -e "    ${BOLD}mkdir -p ~/.config/fish${NC}"
            echo -e "    ${BOLD}echo 'fish_add_path ${install_dir}' >> \$HOME/.config/fish/config.fish${NC}"
        elif [[ -n "$shell_config" ]]; then
            echo -e "    ${BOLD}echo 'export PATH=\"${install_dir}:\$PATH\"' >> ${shell_config}${NC}"
        else
            echo -e "  Add this to your shell config:"
            echo ""
            echo -e "    ${BOLD}export PATH=\"${install_dir}:\$PATH\"${NC}"
            echo ""
            echo -e "  Restart your terminal, then run ${BOLD}entire${NC} to get started."
            exit 0
        fi
        echo ""
        echo -e "  Restart your terminal, then run ${BOLD}entire${NC} to get started."
        exit 0
    fi

    info "Running post-install actions..."
    "$install_path" curl-bash-post-install
}

main "$@"

20		versioninfo.Load()
21	
22		// Create context that cancels on interrupt
23		ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
24	
25		// Handle interrupt signals
26		sigChan := make(chan os.Signal, 1)
27		signals := []os.Signal{os.Interrupt}
28		if runtime.GOOS != "windows" {
29			signals = append(signals, syscall.SIGTERM)
30		}
31		signal.Notify(sigChan, signals...)
32		go func() {
33			<-sigChan
34			cancel()
35		}()
36	
37		// Create and execute root command
38		rootCmd := cli.NewRootCmd()
39	
40		// Make managed-installed plugins discoverable by the kubectl-style
41		// dispatcher: prepend the managed bin dir to PATH before resolution.
42		// Idempotent and silent on failure (managed installs simply won't be
43		// found this run; PATH-installed plugins still work). The closure
44		// restores PATH so built-in commands and their subprocesses don't
45		// inherit the prepended dir. When a plugin runs, we skip the restore
46		// — the os.Exit ends the process, and the plugin child intentionally
47		// inherits the prepended PATH so it can spawn sibling managed plugins.
48		restorePATH := cli.PrependPluginBinDirToPATH(ctx)
49	
50		if handled, code := cli.MaybeRunPlugin(ctx, rootCmd, os.Args[1:]); handled {
51			cancel()
52			os.Exit(code)
53		}
54		restorePATH()
55	
56		executed, err := rootCmd.ExecuteContextC(ctx)
57		if err != nil {
58			var silent *cli.SilentError
59	
60			switch {
61			case errors.As(err, &silent):
62				// Command already printed the error
63			case strings.Contains(err.Error(), "unknown command") || strings.Contains(err.Error(), "unknown flag"):
64				showSuggestion(rootCmd, err)
65			case isPositionalArgError(err):
66				// Arg-count errors come from cobra's own validators (e.g.
67				// cobra.ExactArgs) and surface as "accepts N arg(s), received M".
68				// Show the failing subcommand's usage so the user sees what it
69				// actually expects — rootCmd's usage isn't useful for a
70				// subcommand-level arg mismatch. ExecuteContextC returns the
71				// deepest matched command, which is the one that failed.
72				showSuggestion(executed, err)
73			default:
74				fmt.Fprintln(rootCmd.OutOrStderr(), err)
75			}
76	
77			cancel()
78			os.Exit(1)
79		}
80		cancel() // Cleanup on successful exit
81	}
82	
83	// isPositionalArgError reports whether err looks like a cobra positional-
84	// arg validator failure. cobra's stock validators (ExactArgs, NoArgs,
85	// MinimumNArgs, MaximumNArgs, RangeArgs) all surface error strings
86	// containing "arg(s)", and that substring doesn't appear in cobra's other
87	// error paths or in the cli's own errors — so it's a stable, cheap
88	// discriminator without reaching into cobra internals.
89	func isPositionalArgError(err error) bool {
90		return strings.Contains(err.Error(), "arg(s)")
91	}
92	
93	func showSuggestion(cmd *cobra.Command, err error) {
94		// Print usage first (brew style)
95		fmt.Fprint(cmd.OutOrStderr(), cmd.UsageString())
96		fmt.Fprintf(cmd.OutOrStderr(), "\nError: Invalid usage: %v\n", err)
97	}

# PR Review: entireio/cli#1306 — Vendor git-remote-entire into the CLI; multi-context auth

**Summary** — Vendors the `entire://` git remote helper from `entiredb` into the CLI (extracted into `cmd/git-remote-entire`), introduces a kubectl-style `contexts.json` model shared with `entiredb`, and wires repo-scoped token exchange (RFC 8693) for git smart-HTTP. The work is large but well-structured, heavily tested, and credentials are handled carefully. Overall: **approve with a few small fixes** — one durability bug in the file-backed token store, one stale legacy-code path note, plus a few nits.

## Security

- `internal/entireclient/tokenstore/file.go:79-90` — `save()` writes the temp file, chmods, closes, and renames, but never calls `tmp.Sync()`. `contexts/contexts.go:331` deliberately syncs before close; this divergence means a power loss between write and rename can leave a zero-length token store on disk. Tokens then look "logged out" silently. Fix: add `tmp.Sync()` after the write (mirror `writeNoLock`).
- `internal/entireclient/discovery/cache.go:128-142` — `writeCacheNoLock` likewise doesn't sync the temp file. Same fix; lower stakes (cache only), but inconsistent within the PR.
- `cmd/git-remote-entire/main.go:77` — `ENTIRE_TLS_SKIP_VERIFY=true` is honored without any stderr warning. Local dev needs it, but an unannounced env var that silently disables TLS verification is the kind of footgun that ends up baked into a CI job. Recommend a one-line stderr notice when set (consistent with the auth-side `requireSecureBaseURL` already being noisy).
- `internal/entireclient/clusterdiscovery/discovery.go:69` — `Discover` hard-codes `https://` for the `/.well-known/entire-cluster.json` probe. The CLI elsewhere honors `--insecure-http-auth` / `ENTIRE_TLS_SKIP_VERIFY`; this path will refuse to discover a plain-http local-dev cluster even when the user opted in. Probably intentional (the manifest is unauthenticated metadata, so MITM matters), but worth confirming.
- `internal/remotehelper/transport/proxy.go:132-149` (checkRedirect) — the same-cluster Authorization-carry policy is correct: explicit strip on out-of-cluster hops (Go's default keys on hostname only, which would have leaked across `host:port` shifts), and reads `via[0].Header.Get("Authorization")` to deliberately re-carry the original credential. The `HostInCluster` suffix check at `discovery/parse_replicas.go:36-40` correctly avoids the `attacker.cluster.example.com` confusion. Good defensive work.
- `internal/remotehelper/httpdebug/redact.go` — three-layer redaction (sensitive headers, URL userinfo, JSON token fields) ordered before truncation; the comment explaining why truncate-first leaks via the regex terminator is the right framing. Tests exist for ordering. No issues.
- `internal/entireclient/httputil/oauth.go:115-117` — OAuth error bodies are exposed as `*OAuthError.Body` (capped at 1024). If a misconfigured AS echoes the rejected `subject_token` in the response body, it could surface in CLI error output and logs. Worth running the existing JSON-token redaction over the body before stashing it in the typed error.
- `cmd/entire/cli/auth/store.go:156-158` — `LookupCurrentToken()` is a behavioral change: it now reads via `ContextStore.GetToken`, which prefers the active context's token **regardless of `baseURL`**. With a cross-core context active, this returns a token whose `iss` doesn't match `api.AuthBaseURL()`. The control-plane callers will then 401 against the wrong core. `auth use` already warns the user about cross-core switching, but `LookupCurrentToken` itself silently delivers a wrong-audience token. Consider returning the legacy entry when the active context's core doesn't match `baseURL`, or fail fast in `ContextStore.GetToken` for that case.

## Performance

- `internal/entireclient/tokenstore/file.go:97-119` — `Get` acquires both an in-process mutex *and* a 5-second cross-process flock for every read. Every git-remote-entire invocation reads the token at least once via `LoginTokenForContext`. Concurrent `git fetch` / `git push` operations across multiple repos will serialize through this single lock. Reasonable for now (the lock is held briefly), but if push concurrency grows you'll want a shared-lock read path.
- `internal/entireclient/repocreds/repocreds.go:91-131` — per-key entry mutex with map-mutex held only for `entryFor` is the right shape. Good de-duplication across concurrent fetches for the same repo.
- `internal/entireclient/httpclient/transport.go:23` — `DefaultDialTimeout = 500ms` is aggressive. Documented as overridable via env var, but in practice clones from anywhere with > 250ms RTT will flap on first connect and rely on failover. Consider doubling the default or basing it on a measured baseline.
- `cmd/git-remote-entire/main.go:86-89` — `httpClient.Timeout: 30 * time.Second` is applied to both cluster discovery and OAuth token exchange. Fine for both; just noting it's not configurable.

## Go best practices

- `internal/entireclient/contexts/contexts.go:286` and `tokenstore/file.go:43` — both print warnings via `fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, ...)` from internal/ packages. The remote helper has `debuglog.Printf` (gated by `ENTIRE_DEBUG`) for exactly this purpose; using `os.Stderr` directly bypasses redirection in tests and produces unsolicited stderr noise in normal operation. Route through `debuglog` or accept an injected writer.
- `internal/remotehelper/githelper/run.go:96-101` — the inner `case line == "":` branch checks `errors.Is(err, io.EOF)`, but the outer `errors.Is(err, io.EOF) && line == ""` at line 43-45 already returns nil in that case. The inner check is dead code. Either remove the `if errors.Is(err, io.EOF)` here, or have the outer block fall through deliberately so this is the single termination point.
- `internal/entireclient/discovery/cache.go:120-125` — silently treating corrupt cache JSON as empty (with `nolint:nilerr`) discards diagnostic info. Worth a `debuglog.Printf` (the package can take a fmt-style debugf, like `clusterdiscovery` does) so cache corruption isn't invisible.
- `cmd/git-remote-entire/main.go:92-94` — `auth.MigrateLegacyLoginContext()` errors are swallowed to debuglog only. Acceptable since legacy fallback still works, but the error message will be invisible to a non-debug user whose migration silently failed. Mention in a `fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, ...)` once when the migration step itself errors (vs the "no legacy token" no-op path).
- `internal/remotehelper/httpdebug/roundtripper.go:58-69` — when debug is on, the entire response body is read into memory before being handed back. Comment notes "debug-only cost" but a 500MB pack response with `ENTIRE_DEBUG=1` will OOM small machines. Bound the read (`io.LimitReader` to e.g. 16MB) and note truncation in the preview.
- `cmd/entire/cli/auth/contexts.go:120-126` — `pickContextName` infinite-loops on `for i := 2; ; i++` if the name space is somehow exhausted (it isn't in practice, but defensively cap the loop).

## Backwards compatibility

- New binary `git-remote-entire` shipped via goreleaser + brew cask. `scripts/install.sh:258-263` handles archive missing the binary with a warning, not an error. The cask declares both binaries as `binaries:`. Good rollout shape.
- `entire login` now dual-writes the legacy keyring entry **and** a `contexts.json` entry (`cmd/entire/cli/login.go:117-128`). Legacy entry remains the control-plane source of truth, so old users are not broken. `MigrateLegacyLoginContext` at `cmd/entire/cli/auth/contexts.go:143-179` handles upgrade-time bridging on first `git clone`. Good.
- `entire logout` is materially different: it now also clears the active `contexts.json` context (`logout.go:117`), and `--all` removes every saved login + cluster binding. The Long description warns about it (`logout.go:41-44`), and `noteRemainingLogins` (line 72-85) explicitly surfaces surviving contexts. This is a user-visible UX shift but well-handled.
- `go.mod` adds `github.com/gofrs/flock v0.13.0`. Standard dep, MIT-licensed. Removes `gopkg.in/check.v1` as indirect. Clean.
- `internal/remotehelper/name.go:10` — `BinaryName = "git-remote-entire"` is referenced as the agent string prefix and the usage text. Stable; rename would orphan the helper. No issue.

## Blocking issues

- **`internal/entireclient/tokenstore/file.go save()` must `tmp.Sync()` before close**, to match `contexts.go writeNoLock` and avoid losing tokens on power loss.
- **`cmd/entire/cli/auth/store.go LookupCurrentToken()`** can return a wrong-audience token when the active context's core differs from `api.AuthBaseURL()`. Either reject the cross-core case here or fall back to the legacy entry when audiences mismatch. The existing `auth use` warning is not load-bearing — non-interactive callers don't see it.

## Suggestions

- Mirror the file-store `Sync` fix in `internal/entireclient/discovery/cache.go writeCacheNoLock`.
- Run JSON-token redaction over `OAuthError.Body` before storing it in the typed error.
- Add a one-line stderr notice when `ENTIRE_TLS_SKIP_VERIFY=true` is honored.
- Remove the dead `errors.Is(err, io.EOF)` check inside `case line == "":` in `githelper/run.go`.
- Cap `httpdebug/roundtripper.go` body read so a `ENTIRE_DEBUG=1` clone doesn't OOM on a large pack.
- Route `os.Stderr` warnings in `tokenstore/file.go` and `contexts/contexts.go` through a debuglog/injected writer.
- Consider raising `DefaultDialTimeout` from 500ms to 1s — failover is great, but the default should not punish users on transcontinental links.

## Questions for the author

- Is the hard-coded `https://` in `clusterdiscovery.Discover` intentional even for local-dev (i.e. you expect operators to put a real cert on dev clusters)? If not, plumb the `--insecure-http-auth` opt-in through there too.
- `LookupCurrentToken`'s new behavior — does the team want a context whose core URL doesn't match `api.AuthBaseURL()` to authenticate control-plane commands at all? The `auth use` warning suggests no, but the code path silently allows it.
- The `30 * time.Second` HTTP client timeout in `cmd/git-remote-entire/main.go` covers both discovery and OAuth exchange. Should those have separate budgets (discovery is fast, exchange could hit a cold AS)?

Next: address the two blocking findings — missing tmp.Sync in tokenstore/file.go save(), and LookupCurrentToken returning wrong-audience tokens across cores. (disable recaps in /config)

# Security review — entireio/cli#1306

Reading this as the threat model rather than a line-audit. The most important question is: **what can an attacker do by crafting a malicious `entire://` URL** (in a README, a third-party repo's `.gitmodules`, a Slack link, or even a typo'd hostname)? Git will execute `git-remote-entire` against any URL it's handed, which makes that the primary trust boundary.

## Highest concern: scoped-JWT exfiltration via X-Entire-Replicas (likely fixable, real impact)

`transport.refreshReplicas` (`proxy.go:330-349`) accepts the `X-Entire-Replicas` header value verbatim and uses each entry as a destination for the next request. `doWithFailover` calls `setAuth(req)` on each, which mints a repo-scoped JWT via `repocreds.Token` and attaches it as `Authorization: Bearer …`.

There is **no check that the advertised replica is in the same cluster** as the URL the user actually typed. `parse_replicas.go ParseReplicas` only trims whitespace; `proxy.go markNodeFailed`/`doWithFailover` consume the URLs as-is. The same-cluster policy in `checkRedirect` covers HTTP redirects but not the replica advertisement, which the helper treats as direct destinations.

Exploit shape:

1. Attacker hosts `https://evil.example.com` and serves a `/.well-known/entire-cluster.json` that lists the user's actual core (e.g. `https://us.auth.entire.io`) — any user with a context for that core is now a viable target.
2. Victim runs `git clone entire://evil.example.com/whatever`.
3. The helper resolves the user's existing context, mints a JWT via the user's real core with `aud=https://evil.example.com/whatever, scope=repo:pull` — fine, that JWT is bound to the attacker.
4. Attacker's `info/refs` response returns `X-Entire-Replicas: https://canarytokens.com/foo, https://attacker-log-collector.example.com`.
5. Helper now POSTs `git-upload-pack` and any subsequent calls to those URLs **with the audience-bound JWT attached**.

The JWT is audience-bound, so the receiving host can't replay it elsewhere. But the JWT still contains identity claims (handle, sub, exp, iss, the user's real core URL) — sent unsolicited to attacker-chosen HTTPS endpoints. That's a classic SSRF-shaped identity-claim exfiltration primitive. With logging-as-a-service URLs this is a real reconnaissance tool, not a theoretical one.

**Fix:** validate every replica URL against `discovery.HostInCluster(replicaURL.Hostname(), p.clusterHost)` before adding it to `p.nodes` — or at least before invoking `setAuth` for it. Same check `checkRedirect` already does for redirects. Apply it in `refreshReplicas` *and* in `coldInfoRefs` where the cold-path 307 promotes `rs` to `p.nodes`.

## Second concern: silent persistent auto-binding from a drive-by clone

`clusterdiscovery.ResolveContextForCluster` (`resolve.go:34-83`) does the right thing on the JWT side — `subject_token` is sent to the user's existing trusted core, not to an attacker-claimed core. But on a successful discovery match it writes `cluster_contexts[evilHost] = <existing context>` to `contexts.json` (`BindCluster`).

That binding is persistent. After one clone of an attacker URL:

- All future operations against `evil.example.com` skip discovery and use the bound context's token directly.
- Combined with the exfiltration above, a single drive-by clone establishes a persistent identity-leak channel: any future `git fetch` against that URL keeps minting JWTs.
- `auth contexts` doesn't show cluster bindings, so users have no UX to notice or revoke them.

**Fix:** at minimum, only auto-bind when the cluster's `.well-known` response was served with a verifiable signal that it's an Entire-managed cluster (a signed manifest, or a cluster identifier the core endorses). Failing that, prompt before persisting the binding, or scope the binding to the lifetime of the invocation. Also surface bindings in `auth contexts` so users can audit them.

## Third concern: HostInCluster suffix match needs a floor on cluster specificity

`discovery/parse_replicas.go:36-40`:

```go
return h == c || strings.HasSuffix(h, "."+c)
```

For `clusterHost = "aws-eu-central-1.entire.io"`, this is correctly bounded. For `clusterHost = "entire.io"`, any subdomain — including ones outside operational control — is "in cluster" and inherits Authorization-preservation across redirects. A misconfigured DNS record or an acquired-then-relinquished subdomain becomes a credential receiver.

Today the cluster host comes from `parsedURL.Host`, which the user typed; so the user can't really exploit themselves here. But combined with the auto-binding above, an attacker who can convince a user to clone *once* from `entire://example.com/repo` (where `example.com` is a registrable suffix the attacker controls) effectively widens the same-cluster trust boundary to "anything `*.example.com`".

**Fix:** require `clusterHost` to have at least one dot beyond the registrable suffix (publicsuffix-list check), or maintain an allowlist of accepted entry-domain shapes, before treating subdomain matches as in-cluster.

## Smaller but worth flagging

- `cmd/entire/cli/auth/store.go:156-158` — `LookupCurrentToken()` returns the active context's token regardless of whether its core matches `api.AuthBaseURL()`. A user who ran `auth use other-core-context` then runs a control-plane command sends a wrong-audience token to the configured auth host. That token is bound, so it 401s rather than leaks privilege — but `auth list`/`status`/`revoke` will surface confusing errors, and a hostile receiver still gets the JWT in cleartext (TLS-protected, but visible to the receiving server's logs/IDS). Same shape as the replica issue, smaller blast radius.

- `internal/entireclient/tokenstore/file.go:67-94` `save()` doesn't `tmp.Sync()` before rename. `contexts.go writeNoLock` does. A crash between write and rename leaves the file empty — the next `git fetch` then sees "no token" and reads the legacy fallback, which might also be gone. Not a confidentiality bug but a durability one with auth-availability impact.

- `internal/entireclient/httputil/oauth.go:115-117` — `OAuthError.Body` captures up to 1024 bytes of the OAuth response on non-2xx. If the AS ever echoes the `subject_token` or other request fields back in an error (some IdPs do), it ends up in the typed error and possibly in user-facing CLI output and crash reports. Run the JSON-token redactor over the body before stashing it.

- `internal/remotehelper/httpdebug/roundtripper.go:58-69` reads the full response body into memory when `ENTIRE_DEBUG=1`. An attacker-controlled cluster can return an arbitrarily large response, OOMing the helper. Not a credential issue but a debug-mode DoS knob. Bound the read.

- `cmd/entire/cli/login.go:148-172` `validateReceivedToken` doesn't verify the JWT signature — it trusts TLS to authenticate the AS. Defensible (signature verification needs the AS's JWKS, which is itself fetched over the same TLS connection), but worth documenting as a deliberate decision rather than an oversight.

- `cmd/git-remote-entire/main.go:77` — `ENTIRE_TLS_SKIP_VERIFY=true` is honored silently. No stderr warning, no telemetry, no opt-in confirmation. The kind of env var that ends up baked into a Dockerfile.

## Net assessment

The auth model is well thought through — audience-binding on scoped tokens, same-cluster redirect policy, legacy fallback for migration, careful redactor ordering. The places it breaks down are at the **edges of the trust boundary**: the helper assumes the cluster URL it's handed is benign, and that anything the cluster says (replica advertisement, `.well-known` response, redirect target) is trustworthy. An attacker who controls the URL controls those edges. The replica exfiltration finding is the one I'd want fixed before this ships; the auto-binding behavior I'd want a UX review on; the suffix-match floor is a defense-in-depth follow-up.
